questions.question_text: Under Rea 701.03, which detail must be disclosed about a property's water supply?
questions.explanation: Rea 701.03 requires disclosure of the water supply type, location, any malfunctions, installation date, and the most recent test date. Monthly bill amounts and pressure readings are not specified requirements.

questions.question_text: A seller has a private well installed in 2010. Under Rea 701.03, which information must be disclosed?
distractors: Only the well depth and flow
questions.explanation: Rea 701.03 requires disclosure of the water supply type, location, any malfunctions, installation date, and most recent test date. Well depth and flow rate, while useful, are not the specific statutory requirements.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 477:4-c, what must a seller disclose about the property's sewage disposal system?
questions.correct_answer: Tank size, type, location, and age
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-c requires the seller to disclose the size of the tank, type of system, its location, malfunctions, the age of the system, the date it was most recently serviced, and the name of the contractor who services it. If any item is unknown, that fact must be stated in writing. Rea 701.05 separately requires listing licensees to gather and convey sewage-system information (location, malfunctions, servicing date, contractor) for 1-4 family homes.

questions.question_text: A seller knows the septic system has had repeated backup issues. Under Rea 701.05, must this be disclosed?
distractors: Only if the buyer specifically asks
Only if system is over 20 years old
questions.explanation: Rea 701.05 specifically requires disclosure of any malfunctions of the sewage disposal system. Repeated backup issues are malfunctions that must be disclosed regardless of the system's age or whether the buyer asks.

questions.question_text: Under Rea 701.04 and RSA 477:4-d, what must be disclosed to a buyer about insulation?
questions.explanation: Rea 701.04 requires the listing licensee to ask the seller for the type and location of insulation and convey that information in writing to the buyer prior to or during preparation of an offer; RSA 477:4-d(c) requires the same 'type and location' disclosure from sellers of 1-4 family dwellings. If the information is not available, that fact must be conveyed in writing. R-values, cost, brand names, and installer details are not required.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 477:4-a, when must environmental hazard disclosures be provided to the buyer?
questions.correct_answer: Before the purchase and sale agreement
distractors: At the closing table during final signing
Within 10 days after the closing date
Only when the buyer formally requests them
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-a requires the seller or seller's agent to give the buyer the statutory notification covering radon, arsenic, lead, PFAS, and flood risk before the purchase and sale contract is executed; the buyer acknowledges receipt by signing.

questions.question_text: A 1965 home is listed for sale. Under RSA 477:4-a, which hazard must the seller specifically disclose?
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-a requires the lead notification for any property that includes a building, regardless of age; the statutory notice explains that paint containing lead may have been used in structures before 1978. Separately, federal law (42 U.S.C. 4852d) requires lead-based paint disclosure for pre-1978 housing, so a 1965 home also triggers the federal disclosure. Asbestos certificates, mold test results, and CO detector age are not required by RSA 477:4-a.

questions.question_text: Which environmental hazard was added to NH seller disclosures in January 2025 via HB 398?
questions.explanation: HB 398, effective January 2025, added PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) to the list of environmental hazards that must be disclosed under RSA 477:4-a. Radon, arsenic, and lead were already required.

questions.question_text: Which substances must a NH seller disclose under RSA 477:4-a before signing the purchase and sale agreement?
distractors: Only radon and lead paint hazards
Only PFAS and mold spore exposure
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-a requires disclosure of radon, arsenic, lead-based paint (pre-1978), and PFAS (added January 2025 via HB 398). All four must be disclosed before the P&S agreement. A general flood-risk notice was also added to RSA 477:4-a effective January 1, 2025 (HB 1320), alongside the four substances.

questions.question_text: A seller fails to provide environmental disclosures and the buyer signs the P&S agreement. What is the status of this transaction?
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-a requires environmental hazard disclosures before the purchase and sale agreement. Failure to provide them is a violation of this statute regardless of whether the buyer signed the P&S. Note that RSA 477:4-a, II provides that the omission does not affect the validity of title and creates no civil liability for the seller or seller's agent, but the statutory notification duty itself was not satisfied.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 477:4-d as amended in July 2024, what must a seller of a 1-4 family property newly disclose?
questions.correct_answer: Whether it is in a FEMA flood zone
distractors: The property's elevation above sea level
History of all water damage claims
questions.explanation: HB 1320 (2024, ch. 236), effective July 19, 2024, added flood-hazard-zone status to RSA 477:4-d — the pre-offer written disclosure for 1-4 family dwellings that has covered private water supply, private sewage disposal, and insulation since 1994. The seller must disclose whether the property is located in a federally designated flood hazard zone, and the buyer signs an acknowledgment.

questions.question_text: A seller lists a single-family home in a FEMA flood hazard zone. Under RSA 477:4-d, when must flood zone disclosure occur?
questions.correct_answer: Prior to or during preparation of the offer
distractors: At the closing appointment during final signing
Within 30 days of listing the property for sale
Only if the buyer formally requests this information
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-d requires the written disclosure to be made prior to or during the preparation of an offer for a 1-4 family dwelling, with the buyer acknowledging receipt by signature. It is not deferred to closing, is not tied to a 30-day listing window, and does not depend on a buyer request.

questions.question_text: RSA 477:4-d flood zone disclosure applies to which property types?
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-d specifically applies to 1-4 family residential properties. Commercial properties and those with five or more units are not covered by this particular flood zone disclosure requirement.

questions.question_text: A six-unit apartment building is located in a FEMA flood zone. Does RSA 477:4-d require the seller to disclose this?
questions.correct_answer: No, it only applies to 1-4 units
distractors: Yes, if any unit is residential
Only if flood insurance is active
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-d requires flood zone disclosure only for 1-4 family residential properties. A six-unit apartment building exceeds this threshold and is not subject to this specific disclosure statute. However, the general flood-risk notification under RSA 477:4-a (effective January 1, 2025) applies to any property that includes a building, so the seller of the six-unit still provides that separate notice before the purchase and sale contract.

questions.question_text: A seller of a single-family home in a FEMA flood zone asks their agent whether flood zone disclosure is required. What is the correct answer?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, RSA 477:4-d requires flood zone disclosure
distractors: No, flood zone disclosure is only voluntary
Only if the buyer requests it in writing
Only if the property has active flood insurance
questions.explanation: RSA 477:4-d requires sellers of 1-4 family residential properties to disclose whether the property is in a FEMA-designated flood hazard zone. This disclosure must be provided in writing prior to or during the preparation of an offer, and the buyer must acknowledge receipt by signing (RSA 477:4-d).
